title: Bar chart
body:
Goal: draw a bar chart of the survey with turtle - and make it readable for everyone.

A good chart never uses color alone: every bar has its name underneath and its number on top.

Steps

  1. Open starter.py and press Run. All the bars are the same height and there are no labels. Not very useful!
  2. TODO 1: make bar_height() scale the value so the biggest bar is MAX_HEIGHT pixels tall.
  3. TODO 2 and TODO 3: write the number on top of each bar and the name underneath, using write_at().

Done looks like: six bars from tallest (Block Craft, 5) to shortest (Space Chess, 1), each with a name and a number.

Extra: chart the genre column instead, or add a y-axis line with tick marks every 1 vote.

hints.label: Hint 1
hints.title: Where to look
hints.html: Run the program and look at the bars. They are all the same height because bar_height() ignores its inputs. After that, look inside the loop in draw_bar_chart for TODO 2 and TODO 3. middle is already worked out for you.

hints.label: Hint 2
hints.title: Try this
hints.html: For the height, make a fraction: this bar's value compared with the biggest value. Multiply that fraction by the tallest allowed height. For the labels, call write_at() with the turtle, an x, a y and some text. Numbers must be turned into text with str().

hints.label: Hint 3
hints.title: Almost there
hints.html: Height: return ____ / ____ * MAX_HEIGHT. Number label: write_at(t, ____, BOTTOM + ____ + 5, str(____)). Name label: write_at(t, ____, BOTTOM - ____, ____). The x for both labels is the middle of the bar.

starter.name: starter.py
starter.raw:
# Bar chart
# Turn the survey counts into a picture. Every bar gets:
#   - a height that matches its number (bigger number = taller bar)
#   - the NAME written under it and the NUMBER written on top,
# so nobody has to tell colors apart to read the chart.

import csv
import turtle

PALETTE = ["#E69F00", "#56B4E9", "#009E73", "#F0E442",
           "#0072B2", "#D55E00", "#CC79A7", "#000000"]
FILENAME = "favorite_games.csv"

BAR_WIDTH = 80
GAP = 25
MAX_HEIGHT = 250      # the tallest bar is this many pixels high
BOTTOM = -150         # y position of the bottom of the bars


def count_games(filename):
    """Read the survey and count votes per game (the 8.1 + 8.2 work)."""
    counts = {}
    with open(filename, newline="") as f:
        for row in csv.DictReader(f):
            game = row["favorite_game"].strip().title()
            if game:
                counts[game] = counts.get(game, 0) + 1
    return counts


def bar_height(value, biggest):
    """Scale a value so the biggest value gets MAX_HEIGHT pixels."""
    # TODO 1: every bar is the same height! Return
    #         value / biggest * MAX_HEIGHT  so the biggest bar is MAX_HEIGHT tall.
    return MAX_HEIGHT


def draw_bar(t, x, height, color):
    """A filled rectangle with its bottom-left corner at (x, BOTTOM)."""
    t.penup()
    t.goto(x, BOTTOM)
    t.setheading(0)
    t.pendown()
    t.fillcolor(color)
    t.begin_fill()
    for side in [BAR_WIDTH, height, BAR_WIDTH, height]:
        t.forward(side)
        t.left(90)
    t.end_fill()


def write_at(t, x, y, text, size=12):
    t.penup()
    t.goto(x, y)
    t.write(text, align="center", font=("Arial", size, "normal"))


def draw_bar_chart(t, counts, title):
    """Draw one labeled bar per item in the counts dictionary."""
    biggest = max(counts.values())
    total_width = len(counts) * (BAR_WIDTH + GAP) - GAP
    x = -total_width / 2
    # biggest bar first: sorted() with key= (from week 5!)
    items = sorted(counts.items(), key=lambda pair: pair[1], reverse=True)
    for i, (name, value) in enumerate(items):
        height = bar_height(value, biggest)
        draw_bar(t, x, height, PALETTE[i % len(PALETTE)])
        middle = x + BAR_WIDTH / 2
        # TODO 2: use write_at() to write str(value) just above the bar
        #         (y = BOTTOM + height + 5)
        # TODO 3: use write_at() to write the name under the bar
        #         (y = BOTTOM - 25)
        x += BAR_WIDTH + GAP
    write_at(t, 0, BOTTOM + MAX_HEIGHT + 40, title, size=18)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    screen = turtle.Screen()
    screen.title("Data detectives: bar chart")
    screen.setup(800, 600)
    screen.tracer(0)
    pen = turtle.Turtle()
    pen.hideturtle()
    votes = count_games(FILENAME)
    draw_bar_chart(pen, votes, "Our favorite games (votes)")
    screen.update()
    turtle.done()
